20.7: They said to him, Because no one has hired us. He said to them, Go ye also into my vineyard, and whatever is right, that you will receive.
20.8: When evening was come, the lord of the vineyard said to his steward, Call the labourers and give them their wages, beginning at the last till you come to the first.
20.9: And those who were hired about the eleventh hour came and received every man a denarius.
20.10: Then came the first, supposing that they would receive more, but they likewise received every man a denarius.
20.11: And when they had received it, they murmured against the master of the house,
20.12: saying, These last have worked only one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden and heat of the day.
20.13: He answered to one of them, saying, Friend, I do you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius?
20.14: Take that which is your due, and go your way. I want to give to the last one as much as to you.
20.15: Is it not lawful for me to do as I please with what belongs to me? Is your eye evil because I am good?
20.16: In like manner the last may be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.
20.17: And Jesus went up to Jerusalem, and took the twelve disciples apart along the way and said to them,
20.18: Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem. And the Son of man will be betrayed to the chief priests and to the scribes, and they will condemn him to death,
20.19: and will deliver him to the Gentiles to be mocked, to be scourged, and to be crucified; and the third day he will rise again.
20.20: Then the mother of Zebedee’s children came to him with her sons, doing reverence to him and desiring a certain thing of him.
20.21: He said to her, What would you like? She answered him, Grant that these my two sons may sit, the one on your right hand and the other on your left hand, in your kingdom.
20.22: Jesus answered and said, You know not what you ask. Are you able to drink of the cup that I must drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I must be baptized with? They answered to him, That we are.
20.23: And he said to them, You shall drink of my cup, and shall be baptized with the baptism that I will be baptized with. But to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give, but is for those for whom it is prepared by my Father.
20.24: And when the ten heard about this, they were indignant at the two brethren.
20.25: But Jesus called them to him and said, You know that the lords of the Gentiles have dominion over them, and those who are great exercise power over them.
20.26: It shall not be this way among you, but whosoever would be great among you, let him minister to you,
20.27: and whoever would be chief, let him be your servant –
20.28: even as the Son of man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life for the redemption of many.
20.29: And as they departed from Jericho, crowds of people followed Jesus.
20.30: And two blind men sitting by the wayside, when they heard Jesus pass by, cried out, saying, Lord Son of David, have mercy on us!
20.31: And the people admonished them to hold their peace. But they cried out all the more, saying, Have mercy on us, Lord Son of David!
20.32: Then Jesus stood still and called them, and said, What do you want me to do for you?
20.33: They said to him, Lord, that our eyes may be opened!
20.34: Jesus had compassion on them and touched their eyes, and immediately their eyes received sight. And they followed him.

21.1: When they drew near to Jerusalem and had come to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two of his disciples,
21.2: saying to them, Go into the town that lies in front of you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and her colt with her. Untie them and bring them to me.
21.3: And if anyone says anything to you, say that the Lord has need of them, and straightaway he will let them go.
21.4: All this was done to fulfil that which was spoken by the prophet, saying:
21.5: Tell ye the daughter of Zion: Behold, your king comes to you, humble and sitting upon a donkey and a colt, the foal of a donkey bred to the yoke.
21.6: The disciples went and did as Jesus told them,
21.7: and brought the donkey and the colt, and put on them their clothes, and set him thereon.
21.8: And many of the people spread their garments in the road. Others cut down branches from the trees and strew them in the road.
21.9: Moreover, the people who went ahead, and also those who came after, cried out, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Hosanna in the highest!
21.10: And when he came to Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this?
21.11: And the people said, This is Jesus, the prophet of Nazareth, a town of Galilee.
21.12: And Jesus went into the temple of God and cast out all the people who sold and bought in the temple, and overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of the people who sold doves,
21.13: and said to them, It is written: My house shall be called the house of prayer. But you have made it a den of thieves.
21.14: And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
21.15: When the chief priests and scribes saw the marvels that he did, and the children calling out in the temple and saying, Hosanna to the Son of David, they were indignant
21.16: and said to him, Do you hear what they say? Jesus said to them, Yea, have you never read: From the mouth of babes and sucklings, you have ordained praise?
21.17: And he left them, and went out of the city to Bethany, and had his lodging there.
21.18: In the morning, as he returned into the city again, he hungered,
21.19: and saw a fig tree by the road, and went to it, and found nothing on it but leaves only, and said to it, Let fruit never grow on you from this time forward. And at once the fig tree withered away.
21.20: And when his disciples saw that, they marvelled, saying, How has the fig tree withered away so suddenly?
21.21: Jesus answered and said to them, Truly I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what I have done to the fig tree, but also if you say to this mountain, Take yourself away and cast yourself into the sea, it will be done.
21.22: And whatever you ask in prayer ( if you believe ), you will receive it.
21.23: And when he had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching and said, By what authority are you doing these things? And who gave you this authority?
21.24: Jesus answered and said to them, I also will ask of you a certain question, which, if you answer me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.
21.25: The baptism of John: whence was it? from heaven, or of men? Then they reasoned among themselves, saying, If we say from heaven, he will say to us, why did you not then believe him?
21.26: But if we say it was of men, then we fear the people. ( For everyone held John to be a prophet. )
21.27: And they answered Jesus and said, We don’t know. And he likewise said to them, Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.
21.28: What do you say to this: A certain man had two sons, and went to the elder and said, Son, go and work today in my vineyard.
21.29: He answered and said, I will not, but afterward he repented and went.
21.30: Then the father went to the second son and said likewise. And he answered and said, I will, Sir. Yet he did not go.
21.31: Which of the two did the will of the father? And they said to him, The first. Jesus said to them, Truly I say to you that the publicans and the harlots shall come into the kingdom of God before you.
21.32: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him. But the publicans and the harlots believed him. And yet you, though you saw it, were still not moved with repentance, so that you might afterward have believed him.
21.33: Hear another similitude: There was a certain householder, who planted a vineyard. He hedged it round about, and made a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country.
21.34: And when the time of the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, to receive the fruits of it.
21.35: And the husbandmen caught his servants, and beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
21.36: Again he sent other servants, more than at the first, and they treated them likewise.
21.37: Then last of all he sent to them his own son, saying, They will respect my son.
21.38: But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us take his inheritance for ourselves.
21.39: And they caught him and thrust him out of the vineyard, and slew him.
21.40: Now when the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do with those husbandmen?
21.41: They said to him, He will miserably destroy those evil persons, and will let out his vineyard to other husbandmen, who will render to him the fruit in their seasons.
21.42: Jesus said to them, Did you never read in the scriptures: The stone which the builders refused, the same is set in the principal part of the corner; this was the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?
21.43: Therefore I say to you, the kingdom of God will be taken from you and will be given to the Gentiles, who will bring forth the fruits of it.
21.44: And whosoever falls on this stone, he shall be broken; but whomever it falls upon, it will grind him to powder.
21.45: When the chief priests and Pharisees heard these similitudes, they perceived that he was speaking of them.
21.46: And they went about to lay hands on him, but they feared the people, because they took him as a prophet.

22.1: And Jesus spoke to them again in similitudes, saying,
22.2: The kingdom of heaven is like a certain king who arranged a marriage for his son,
22.3: and sent forth his servants to call those who were bid to the wedding, and they would not come.
22.4: Again he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell those who are bidden, Behold, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and my fatted calves are killed, and all things are ready. Come to the marriage.
22.5: But they made light of it and went their ways, one to his farmstead, another about his wares.
22.6: The rest took his servants and shamefully abused them, and slew them.
22.7: When the king heard about this, he was furious, and sent forth his warriors, and destroyed those murderers, and burnt up their city.
22.8: Then said the king to his servants, The wedding was prepared, but those who were bidden were not worthy.
22.9: Go therefore out into the highways, and as many as you find, bid them to the marriage.
22.10: The servants went out into the highways and gathered together as many as they could find, both good and bad, and the wedding was furnished with guests.
22.11: Then the king came in to visit the guests, and spotted there a man who did not have on a wedding garment,
22.12: and said to him, Friend, how did it happen that you came in here and do not have on a wedding garment? And the man was quite speechless.
22.13: Then said the king to his servants, Take and bind him hand and foot, and cast him into outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
22.14: For many are called, but few are chosen.
22.15: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel, how they might tangle him in his words.
22.16: And they sent to him their disciples with Herod’s servants, saying, Master, we know that you are true, and teach the way of God truly, neither mind any person, for you do not consider men’s estate.
22.17: Tell us therefore what you think: is it lawful to remit tribute to Caesar, or not?
22.18: Jesus perceived their wickedness and said, Why do you bait me, you hypocrites?
22.19: Let me see the tribute coin. So they brought him a denarius.
22.20: And he said to them, Whose image and superscription is this?
22.21: They said to him, Caesar’s. Then he said to them, Give therefore to Caesar that which is Caesar’s, and give to God that which is God’s.
22.22: When they heard that, they marvelled, and left him and went their way.
22.23: The same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him and asked him,
22.24: saying, Teacher, Moses said that if a man dies having no children, the brother should marry the widow and raise up seed for his brother.
22.25: There were with us seven brethren. The first married and died without issue, and left his wife to his brother.
22.26: Likewise the second and the third, down to the seventh.
22.27: Last of all the woman died also.
22.28: Now in the resurrection, whose wife will she be of the seven? For they all had her.
22.29: Jesus answered and said to them, You are deceived, and do not understand the scriptures, nor yet the power of God.
22.30: For in the resurrection people neither marry nor are married, but are as the angels in heaven.
22.31: As for the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what is spoken to you by God, who says,
22.32: I am Abraham’s God, and Isaac’s God, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.
22.33: And when the people heard that, they were astonished at his teaching.
22.34: When the Pharisees heard how he had put the Sadducees to silence, they drew together.
22.35: One of them, who was a doctor of the law, asked him a question, testing him and saying,
22.36: Teacher, which is the chief commandment in the law?
22.37: Jesus said to him, Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind;
22.38: this is the first and the chief commandment.
22.39: And there is another like this: Love your neighbour as yourself.
22.40: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
22.41: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them,
22.42: saying, What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he? They said to him, The son of David.
22.43: He said to them, How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,
22.44: The Lord said to my Lord, Sit on my right hand, till I make your enemies your footstool?
22.45: If David calls him Lord, how is he then his son?
22.46: And no one could answer him a word. Neither did anyone from that day forth dare ask him any more questions.

23.1: Then Jesus spoke to the people and to his disciples,
23.2: saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.
23.3: All therefore that they bid you to observe, that observe and do. But do not follow their works. For they say, but do not do.
23.4: Yea and they bind up heavy burdens, grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders, but they will not lift a finger to carry them themselves.
23.5: All their works they do to be seen by men. They enlarge their phylacteries, and make large borders on their garments.
23.6: They love to sit uppermost at feasts, and to have the chief seats in the synagogues,
23.7: and greetings in the markets, and to be called Rabbi by men.
23.8: But you shall not suffer yourselves to be called Rabbi. For one is your Master, that is, Christ, and you are all brethren.
23.9: And call no man upon the earth your father, for there is but one your Father, and he is in heaven.
23.10: Do not be called teachers, for there is but one your Teacher, and he is Christ.
23.11: He who is greatest among you will be your servant.
23.12: But whosoever exalts himself, shall be brought low. And he who humbles himself, shall be exalted.
23.13: Woe is to you scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you shut up the kingdom of heaven before men. You yourselves go not in, neither do you suffer those who come to enter in.
23.14: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You devour widows’ houses, and that under a colour of praying long prayers, for which you shall receive the greater damnation.
23.15: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who compass land and sea to bring one person into your belief. And when he is brought in, you make him twofold more the child of hell than you yourselves are.
23.16: Woe to you, blind guides, who say that if someone swears by the temple, it is nothing, but whosoever swears by the gold of the temple, he offends.
23.17: O fools, and blind! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that sanctifies the gold?
23.18: And whosoever swears by the altar, it is nothing, but whoever swears by the offering that lies on the altar, offends –
23.19: Ye fools, and blind! Which is greater: the offering, or the altar that sanctifies the offering?
23.20: Whoever therefore swears by the altar, swears by it and by all that is on it.
23.21: And whoever swears by the temple, swears by it and by him who dwells therein.
23.22: And he who swears by heaven, swears by the seat of God and by him who sits upon it.
23.23: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who tithe mint, anise, and cummin, and leave the weightier matters of the law undone: judgment, mercy, and faith. These you ought to have done, and not to have left the others undone.
23.24: Blind guides, who strain out a gnat and swallow a camel!
23.25: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of greed and excess.
23.26: You blind Pharisee: cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter, so that the outside of them may be clean also.
23.27: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like painted tombs, which appear beautiful outwardly, but within are full of dead bones and of all uncleanness.
23.28: This is how you are, for outwardly you appear righteous to men, when within you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
23.29: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You build the tombs of the prophets, and adorn the sepulchres of the righteous,
23.30: and say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in the blood of the prophets.
23.31: So then, you are witnesses against yourselves, that you are the children of those who killed the prophets!
23.32: Fill up then likewise the cup of your fathers.
23.33: Serpents and offspring of vipers, how can you escape the judgment of hell?
23.34: And so behold: I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,
23.35: so that upon you may come all the righteous blood that was shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, whom you slew between the temple and the altar.
23.36: Truly I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.
23.37: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills prophets, and stones those who are sent to you! How often would I have gathered your children together, as the hen gathers her chicks under her wings. But you would not.
23.38: Behold, your habitation shall be left to you desolate.
23.39: For I say to you, you will not see me henceforth until you say, Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.

24.1: And Jesus went out and departed from the temple, and his disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.
24.2: Jesus said to them, Do you not see all these things? Truly I say to you, there shall not be left here one stone upon another that will not be cast down.
24.3: And as he sat on the Mount of Olives, his disciples came to him privately, saying, Tell us when these things will be, and what sign will be of your coming, and of the end of the world.
24.4: And Jesus answered and said to them, Take heed that no one deceives you.
24.5: For many will come in my name saying, I am Christ! and will deceive many.
24.6: You will hear of wars and of the infamy of wars. But see that you be not troubled. For all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.
24.7: For nation will rise against nation, and realm against realm. And there will be pestilence, hunger, and earthquakes in all quarters.
24.8: All these are the beginning of sorrows.
24.9: Then they will put you to tribulation, and will kill you, and you will be hated by all nations for my name’s sake.
24.10: And then shall many fall into offence, and will betray one another, and will hate one another.
24.11: And many false prophets will arise, and will deceive many.
24.12: And because iniquity will have the upper hand, the love of many will abate.
24.13: But he who endures to the end, the same will be saved.
24.14: And this glad tidings of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world, for a witness to all nations; and then shall the end come.
24.15: When you therefore see the abomination that betokens desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet stand in the holy place, let him who reads it, understand it.
24.16: Then let those who are in Judea flee into the mountains.
24.17: And let him who is on the housetop not come down to fetch anything out of his house.
24.18: Neither let him who is in the field return back to fetch his clothes.
24.19: Woe shall be in those days to women that are with child, and to those who give suck.
24.20: But pray that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the Sabbath day.
24.21: For then will be great tribulation, such as was not from the beginning of the world to this time, nor will be.
24.22: Yea and unless those days were shortened, no flesh would be saved. But for the sake of the chosen, those days will be shortened.
24.23: Then if any one says to you, See, here is Christ! or there is Christ! – believe it not.
24.24: For false christs and false prophets will arise, and will do great miracles and wonders, insomuch that if it were possible, the very elect should be deceived.
24.25: Take heed, I have told you beforehand.
24.26: So if they say to you, Behold, he is in the desert! go not forth; or, Behold, he is in the secret places! believe it not.
24.27: For as the lightning comes out of the east and shines to the west, so will the coming of the Son of man be.
24.28: For wherever the dead body is, there will the eagles resort.
24.29: Immediately after the tribulations of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give her light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven shall move.
24.30: And then will appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven. And then shall all the kindreds of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man come in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
24.31: And he will send his angels with the great voice of a trumpet, and they will gather together his chosen from the four winds, and from the one end of the world to the other.
24.32: Learn from a similitude of the fig tree: when its branches are yet tender and its leaves sprung, you know that summer is near.
24.33: So likewise you, when you see all these things, may be sure that it is near, even at the doors.
24.34: Truly I say to you that this generation shall not pass till all these things be fulfilled.
24.35: Heaven and earth shall perish, but my words will abide.
24.36: But of that day and hour no man knows – no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
24.37: As the time of Noah was, so likewise will the coming of the Son of man be.
24.38: For as in the days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and were married, right up to the day that Noah entered into the ship,
24.39: and knew of nothing till the flood came and took them all away, so also will the coming of the Son of man be.
24.40: Then two will be in the fields; the one will be received, and the other will be refused.
24.41: Two will be grinding at the mill; the one will be received, and the other will be refused.
24.42: Watch therefore, because you do not know what hour your master will come.
24.43: Of this be sure: if the householder knew what hour the thief would come, he would surely watch, and not allow his house to be broken into.
24.44: Therefore you also be ready, because in the hour you think he would not, the Son of man will come.
24.45: If there be any servant faithful and wise, whom his master has appointed over his household, to give them food in due season,
24.46: happy is that servant whom his master ( when he comes ) finds so doing.
24.47: Truly I say to you, he will appoint him over all his goods.
24.48: But if the evil servant says in his heart, My master will defer his coming,
24.49: and begins to smite his fellow servants, yea and to eat and to drink with the drunken,
24.50: the servant’s master will come in a day when he is not expecting him, and in an hour that he is not aware of,
24.51: and will separate him, and give him his reward with the hypocrites. And there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

25.1: Then the kingdom of heaven will be likened to ten virgins who took their lamps and went to meet the bridegroom.
25.2: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
25.3: The foolish took their lamps, but took no oil with them.
25.4: But the wise took oil with them in their vessels, with their lamps also.
25.5: While the bridegroom tarried, all slumbered and slept.
25.6: And right at midnight there was a cry made: Behold, the bridegroom comes! Go out to meet him!
25.7: Then all those virgins arose and prepared their lamps.
25.8: And the foolish said to the wise, Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.
25.9: But the wise answered, saying, Not so, lest there not be enough for us and you; but go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.
25.10: And while they were going to buy, the bridegroom came. And those who were ready went in with him to the wedding, and the gate was shut up.
25.11: Afterwards came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us!
25.12: But he answered and said, Truly I say to you, I know you not.
25.13: Watch, therefore. For you know neither the day nor yet the hour when the Son of man will come.
25.14: Likewise it will be as a certain man, ready to take his journey to a strange country, called his servants and delivered his goods to them.
25.15: And to one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one – to every man according to his ability – and straightaway departed.
25.16: Then he who had received the five talents went and traded with them, and won another five talents.
25.17: Likewise, he who received two gained another two.
25.18: But he who received the one went and dug a hole in the earth, and hid his master’s money.
25.19: After a long season, the lord of those servants came and reckoned with them.
25.20: Then came he that had received five talents, and brought another five talents, saying, Master, you delivered to me five talents; here, I have gained with them five talents more.
25.21: Then his master said to him, Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful in a little; I will appoint you over much. Enter into your master’s joy!
25.22: Also he who received two talents came and said, Master, you delivered to me two talents; here, I have won two other talents with them.
25.23: And his master said to him, Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful in a little; I will appoint you over much. Go in, into your master’s joy.
25.24: Then he who had received the one talent came and said, Master, I considered that you were a hard man, who reaps where you did not sow and gathers where you did not scatter,
25.25: and was therefore afraid, and went and hid your talent in the earth. Here, have your talent.
25.26: His master answered and said to him, You evil servant, and slothful: you knew that I reap where I did not sow, and gather where I did not scatter?
25.27: You ought therefore to have put my money with the moneychangers, and then at my coming I would have received what is my own with profit.
25.28: Take therefore the talent from him, and give it to the one who has ten talents.
25.29: For every person who has will be given more, and he will have abundance; and from him who has not, shall be taken away even what he has.
25.30: And cast that unprofitable servant into outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
25.31: When the Son of man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the seat of his glory.
25.32: And before him shall be gathered all nations. And he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides the sheep from the goats.
25.33: And he will set the sheep on his right hand and the goats on the left.
25.34: Then shall the king say to those on his right hand, Come ye blessed children of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world.
25.35: For I was hungry and you gave me food. I was thirsty and you gave me drink. I was homeless and you lodged me.
25.36: I was naked and you clothed me. I was sick and you visited me. I was in prison and you came to me.
25.37: Then the righteous will answer him, saying, Master, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink?
25.38: When did we see you homeless and lodge you, or naked and clothe you?
25.39: Or when did we see you sick, or in prison, and come to you?
25.40: And the king will answer and say to them, Truly I say to you, inasmuch as you did it for one of the least of these my brethren, you did it for me.
25.41: Then shall the king say to those who will be on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, which is prepared for the devil and his angels.
25.42: For I was hungry and you gave me no food. I was thirsty and you gave me no drink.
25.43: I was homeless and you did not lodge me. I was naked and you did not clothe me. I was sick, and in prison, and you did not visit me.
25.44: Then they also will answer him, saying, Master, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or homeless, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister to you?
25.45: Then shall he answer them and say, Truly I say to you, inasmuch as you did it not for one of the least of these, you did it not for me.
25.46: And these shall go into everlasting pain, but the righteous into life eternal.

26.1: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these sayings, he said to his disciples,
26.2: You know that after two days will be the Passover. And the Son of man will be delivered to be crucified.
26.3: Then the chief priests, scribes, and elders of the people assembled together at the palace of the high priest called Caiaphas
26.4: and held a council, how they might take Jesus by subtlety and kill him.
26.5: But, they said, not on the holy day, lest any uproar arise among the people.
26.6: When Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
26.7: there came to him a woman who had an alabaster jar of precious anointing oil, and poured it on his head as he sat at the board.
26.8: When his disciples saw that, they were indignant, saying, Why this waste?
26.9: This oyntment might well have been sold, and the money given to the poor.
26.10: When Jesus understood this he said to them, Why do you trouble the woman? She has wrought a good work upon me.
26.11: For you will have poor folk always with you, but me you will not have always.
26.12: And in that she poured this oyntment on my body, she did it to bury me with.
26.13: Truly I say to you, wherever this gospel is preached throughout all the world, there also will this that she has done be told, for a memorial of her.
26.14: Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
26.15: and said, What will you give me, and I will deliver him to you? And they agreed with him for thirty pieces of silver.
26.16: And from that time, he sought an opportunity to betray him.
26.17: On the first day of sweet bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying to him, Where would you have us prepare for you to eat the Passover lamb?
26.18: And he said, Go into the city to a certain man, and say to him, The Master says, My time is at hand; I will keep my Passover at your place with my disciples.
26.19: And the disciples did as Jesus had directed them, and made ready the Passover lamb.
26.20: When the evening was come, he sat down with the twelve.
26.21: And as they were eating he said, Truly I say to you that one of you will betray me.
26.22: And they were exceeding sorrowful, and began every one of them to say to him, Is it I, Master?
26.23: He answered and said, He who dips his hand with me in the dish, the same will betray me.
26.24: The Son of man goes as it is written of him. But woe is to that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed. It would have been good for that man if he had never been born.
26.25: Then Judas who betrayed him answered and said, Is it I, Master? Jesus said to him, You have said it.
26.26: As they were eating, Jesus took bread and gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to the disciples and said, Take, eat; this is my body.
26.27: And he took the cup, and thanked, and gave it to them, saying, Drink of it, everyone.
26.28: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.
26.29: I say to you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine until that day when I shall drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.
26.30: And when they had sung praises, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
26.31: Then Jesus said to them, You will all fall away because of me this night. For it is written: I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered abroad.
26.32: But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.
26.33: Peter answered and said to him, Even if everyone were to fall away because of you, yet I would never fall away.
26.34: Jesus said to him, Truly I say to you that this same night, before the cock crows, you will deny me three times.
26.35: Peter said to him, If I had to die with you, yet I would not deny you. Likewise also said all the disciples.
26.36: Then Jesus went with them to a place which is called Gethsemane, and said to the disciples, Sit here while I go and pray yonder.
26.37: And he took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful, and to be in an agony.
26.38: Then said Jesus to them, My soul is heavy, even unto death. You stay here, and watch with me.
26.39: And he went a little apart and fell flat on his face and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as you will.
26.40: And he came back to the disciples and found them asleep, and said to Peter, What, could you not watch with me for one hour?
26.41: Watch, and pray that you do not fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.
26.42: He went away once more and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup cannot pass away from me but that I drink of it, thy will be fulfilled.
26.43: And he came and found his disciples asleep again. For their eyes were heavy.
26.44: And he left them and went again and prayed the third time, saying the same words.
26.45: Then he came to his disciples and said to them, Sleep on now, and take your rest! Take heed: the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
26.46: Arise, let us be going. Behold, he who betrays me is at hand.
26.47: While he was yet speaking, lo, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a large band of men bearing swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders of the people.
26.48: And he who betrayed him had arranged a sign, saying, Whomever I kiss, he is the one; lay hands on him.
26.49: And at once he went up to Jesus and said, Hail, Master! and kissed him.
26.50: And Jesus said to him, Friend, why have you come? Then they came and laid hands on Jesus and took him.
26.51: And at that, one of the men who were with Jesus stretched out his hand and drew his sword, and struck a servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
26.52: Then said Jesus to him, Put your sword back in its sheath. For all who take the sword will perish by the sword.
26.53: Or do you think I cannot now pray to my Father, and he would send me more than twelve legions of angels?
26.54: But how then would the scriptures be fulfilled? For this is how it must be.
26.55: At the same time Jesus said to the throng, You have come out as if against a thief, with swords and clubs to take me. I sat daily teaching in the temple among you, and you did not take me.
26.56: All this was done so that the scriptures of the prophets may be fulfilled.
26.57: Then all the disciples forsook him and fled. And they took Jesus and led him to Caiaphas, the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were assembled.
26.58: And Peter followed him from afar off to the high priest’s palace, and went in and sat with the servants, to see the end of it.
26.59: The chief priests and the elders and all the council sought false witness against Jesus in order to put him to death,
26.60: but found none. Though many false witnesses came forward, yet they found none. At the last came two false witnesses,
26.61: and said, This fellow said, I can destroy the temple of God and build it again in three days.
26.62: And the chief priest arose and said to Jesus, Do you answer nothing? How is it that these men bear witness against you?
26.63: But Jesus held his peace. And the chief priest spoke and said to him, I charge you in the name of the living God to tell us if you are Christ, the Son of God.
26.64: Jesus said to him, It is as you have said. But I say to you, hereafter you will see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and come in the clouds of the sky.
26.65: Then the high priest tore his clothes, saying, He has blasphemed! Why do we need any more witnesses? Here, now you have heard his blasphemy.
26.66: What do you think? They answered and said, He is worthy to die.
26.67: Then they spat in his face and buffeted him with fists. And others struck him with the palm of their hands on the face,
26.68: saying, Tell us, Christ, who is it that hit you?
26.69: Peter was sitting out in the centre courtyard. And a maidservant came to him, saying, You also were with Jesus of Galilee.
26.70: But he denied it before them all, saying, I don’t know what you are saying.
26.71: When he had gone out into the porch, another servant girl saw him and said to the people who were there, This fellow was also with Jesus of Nazareth.
26.72: And again Peter denied with an oath that he knew the man.
26.73: And after a while, some people standing nearby came up and said to Peter, Surely you are also one of them, for your speech gives you away.
26.74: Then he began to curse, and to swear that he did not know the man. And immediately the cock crew.
26.75: And Peter remembered the words of Jesus, who had said to him, Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times. And he went out at the doors and wept bitterly.

27.1: When the morning was come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people held a council against Jesus, to put him to death,
27.2: and brought him bound, and delivered him to Pontius Pilate the governor.
27.3: Then when Judas who had betrayed him saw that he was condemned, he repented, and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
27.4: saying, I have sinned, betraying the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? You see to it.
27.5: And Judas cast down the silver pieces in the temple and departed, and went and hanged himself.
27.6: And the chief priests took the silver pieces and said, It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.
27.7: And they took counsel, and bought with the money a potter’s field to bury strangers in.
27.8: Therefore that field is called the Field of Blood until this day.
27.9: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, saying: And they took thirty silver pieces, the price of him that was sold, whom they bought from the children of Israel,
27.10: and gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord appointed me.
27.11: Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor asked him, saying, Are you the king of the Jews? Jesus said to him, It is as you say.
27.12: And when he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.
27.13: Then Pilate said to him, Do you not hear how many things they lay against you?
27.14: And he answered him never a word, insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.
27.15: At that feast the governor was accustomed to release to the people a prisoner, whomever they would request.
27.16: He had then a notable prisoner called Barabbas.
27.17: And when the people were gathered together, Pilate said to them, Which do you want me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?
27.18: For he knew well that it was for envy they had delivered him.
27.19: When he was seated to give judgment, his wife sent to him, saying, Have nothing to do with that just man. For I have suffered many things this day in a dream about him.
27.20: But the chief priests and the elders had persuaded the people that they should ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus.
27.21: Then the governor spoke and said to them, Which of the two do you want me to set free to you? And they said, Barabbas!
27.22: Pilate said to them, What shall I do then with Jesus who is called Christ? They all said to him, Let him be crucified!
27.23: Then said the governor, What evil has he done? And they cried out all the more, saying, Let him be crucified!
27.24: When Pilate saw that he was not prevailing, but that more of a tumult was made, he took water and washed his hands before the people, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person, and that you should see.
27.25: Then all the people answered and said, His blood be on us and on our children!
27.26: Then he let Barabbas go free to them, and had Jesus scourged, and delivered him to be crucified.
27.27: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus to the common hall, and gathered to him the whole company of soldiers.
27.28: And they stripped him and put on him a purple robe,
27.29: and plaited a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand. And they bowed their knees before him and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!
27.30: And they spat upon him, and took the reed and struck him on the head.
27.31: And when they had mocked him, they took the robe back from him and put his own clothes on him, and led him away to crucify him.
27.32: And as they went out, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon; him they compelled to bear his cross.
27.33: And when they came to the place called Golgotha ( which means, a place of dead mens’ skulls ),
27.34: they gave him vinegar to drink mixed with gall. But when he had tasted of it, he would not drink.
27.35: When they had crucified him, they parted his garments and cast lots, to fulfil that which was spoken by the prophet: They divided my garments among them, and for my vesture did cast lots.
27.36: And they sat and kept watch over him there.
27.37: And they set up over his head his accusation, written this is jesus, the king of the jews.
27.38: And there were two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand and another on the left.
27.39: The people who passed by reviled him, wagging their heads
27.40: and saying, You who destroy the temple of God and build it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!
27.41: Likewise also the high priests, mocking him with the scribes and elders, said,
27.42: He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he really is the king of Israel, let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe him.
27.43: He trusted in God – let him deliver him now, if he will have him. For he said, I am the Son of God.
27.44: Also the thieves who were crucified with him cast the same in his teeth.
27.45: From the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
27.46: And about the ninth hour, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? ( which means, My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? )
27.47: Some of the people who were standing there, when they heard that, said, This man is calling for Elijah!
27.48: And straightaway one of them ran and took a sponge, and filled it full of vinegar and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.
27.49: Others said, Leave him be; let us see if Elijah will come and deliver him.
27.50: Jesus cried out again with a loud voice, and yielded up the spirit.
27.51: And behold: the veil of the temple did tear in two, from the top to the bottom, and the earth did quake, and the rocks did split.
27.52: And graves did open, and the bodies of many saints who slept arose,
27.53: and came out of the graves after his resurrection, and came into the holy city and appeared to many.
27.54: When the centurion and those who were with him watching Jesus saw the earthquake and those things that happened, they feared greatly, saying, Surely this was the Son of God.
27.55: And many women were there, watching him from afar – those who had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering to him.
27.56: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s children.
27.57: When the evening was come, there came a rich man of Arimathea named Joseph, which man also was Jesus’ disciple.
27.58: He went to Pilate and requested the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be delivered.
27.59: And Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
27.60: and put it in his new tomb, which he had hewn out even in the rock. He rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre and departed.
27.61: And there were Mary Magdalene and the other Mary, sitting across from the sepulchre.
27.62: The next day, which followed the day of preparing the Sabbath, the high priests and Pharisees assembled before Pilate
27.63: and said, Sir, we remember what this deceiver said while he was still alive: After three days, I will arise again.
27.64: Command therefore that the sepulchre be made secure until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come and steal him away, and say to the people that he is risen from the dead, and the last error be worse than the first.
27.65: Pilate said to them, Take watchmen; go and make it as secure as you can.
27.66: And they went and made the sepulchre secure with watchmen, and sealed the stone.

28.1: At the close of the Sabbath day, which is in the dawn of the morrow after the Sabbath, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the sepulchre.
28.2: And behold, there was a great earthquake. For the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door and sat upon it.
28.3: His countenance was like lightening, and his raiment white as snow.
28.4: And for fear of him the guards were overwhelmed, and became as dead men.
28.5: The angel spoke and said to the women, Fear not: I know that you seek Jesus, who was crucified.
28.6: He is not here. He is risen, as he said. Come and see the place where the Lord was put.
28.7: And go quickly and tell his disciples that he is risen from death. And behold, he will go before you into Galilee; there you will see him. Lo, I have told you.
28.8: And they departed quickly from the sepulchre with fear and great joy, and did run to bring his disciples word.
28.9: And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, All Hail! And they came and held him by the feet and worshipped him.
28.10: Then said Jesus to them, Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brethren to go into Galilee, and there they will see me.
28.11: When they had gone, some of the guards went into the city and told to the high priests all the things that had happened.
28.12: And they gathered them together with the elders and took counsel, and gave a large sum of money to the soldiers,
28.13: saying, Say that his disciples came by night and stole him away while you slept.
28.14: And if this comes to the governor’s ears, we will appease him and keep you out of trouble.
28.15: And the soldiers took the money and did as they were instructed. And this story is circulated among the Jews to this day.
28.16: Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, to a mountain where Jesus had directed them.
28.17: And when they saw him, they worshipped him. But some of them doubted.
28.18: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, All power is given to me in heaven and in earth.
28.19: Go therefore and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit,
28.20: and teaching them to observe all things, whatsoever I commanded you. And lo, I am with you always, even until the end of the world. Here ends the gospelof St. Matthew.

1.1: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God,
1.2: as it is written in the prophets: Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who shall prepare your way before you.
1.3: The voice of a crier in the wilderness: Prepare ye the way of the Lord; make his paths straight!
1.4: John baptized in the wilderness, and preached the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.
1.5: And all the countryside of Judea and the people of Jerusalem went out to him, and were all baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.
1.6: John was clothed with camel’s hair, and with a girdle of skin about his loins. And he ate locusts and wild honey,
1.7: and preached, saying, One mightier than I comes after me, whose shoe latchet I am not worthy to stoop down and loose.
1.8: I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.
1.9: And it came to pass in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth, a town of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan River.
1.10: And as soon as Jesus came out of the water, John saw heaven open, and the Holy Spirit descending upon him like a dove.
1.11: And there came a voice from heaven: You are my dear Son, in whom I delight.
1.12: And immediately the Spirit drove him into the wilderness.
1.13: And he was there in the wilderness forty days, and was tried by Satan, and was with wild creatures. And the angels ministered to him.
1.14: After John was taken, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God
1.15: and saying, The time has come, and the kingdom of God is at hand. Repent, and believe the gospel!
1.16: As he walked by the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and John his brother casting nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
1.17: And Jesus said to them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
1.18: And straightaway they left their nets and followed him.
1.19: And when he had gone a little further, he saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother as they were in the boat mending their nets.
1.20: And right away he called them. And they left their father Zebedee in the boat with his hired servants, and went their way after him.
1.21: And they entered into Capernaum. And straightaway on the Sabbath days he entered into the synagogue and taught.
1.22: And the people marvelled at his teaching. For he taught them as one who had power with him, and not as the scribes.
1.23: And there was in their synagogue a man vexed with an unclean spirit, who cried out,
1.24: saying, Let us be! What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know you, who you are: even the Holy One of God.
1.25: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold your peace and come out of him!
1.26: And the unclean spirit tore the man and cried out with a loud voice, and came out of him.
1.27: And they were all amazed, insomuch that they questioned one another among themselves, saying, What thing is this? What new doctrine is this? For he commands the foul spirits with power, and they obey him.
1.28: And immediately his fame spread abroad throughout all the region bordering on Galilee.
1.29: And directly, as soon as they had left the synagogue, they entered into the house of Simon and Andrew with James and John.
1.30: And Simon’s mother - in - law lay sick of a fever. And right away they told him of her.
1.31: And he came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. And the fever left her immediately, and she ministered to them.
1.32: And in the evening, when the sun was down, people brought to him all their sick and those that were possessed with devils.
1.33: And all the city gathered together at the door.
1.34: And he healed many who were sick of different diseases. And he cast out many devils, and would not permit the devils to speak, because they knew him.
1.35: And in the morning very early, Jesus arose and went out to a solitary place, and there prayed.
1.36: And Simon and those who were with him followed after Jesus.
1.37: And when they had found him, they said to him, All the people are searching for you.
1.38: He said to them, Let us go into the next towns so that I can preach there also; for truly, I came out for that purpose.
1.39: And he preached in their synagogues throughout all Galilee, and cast the devils out.
1.40: And there came a leper to him, beseeching him, who kneeled down to him and said to him, If you will, you can make me clean.
1.41: And Jesus had compassion on him, and put forth his hand, touched him, and said to him, I will; be clean.
1.42: And as soon as he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him and he was cleansed.
1.43: And Jesus charged the man, and sent him away directly,
1.44: and said to him, See that you say nothing to anyone, but go and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing those things that Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.
1.45: But the man ( as soon as he had left ) began to talk freely, and to tell everyone what had been done, so that Jesus could no longer openly enter into the towns, but was out in the country. And people came to him from every quarter.

2.1: After a few days he entered into Capernaum again, and it was rumoured that he was in a house.
2.2: And soon many gathered together, insomuch that now there was no room to receive them, no, not so much as about the door. And he preached the word to them.
2.3: And there came to him people bringing a paralytic, borne by four men.
2.4: And because they could not come near to him for the press, they uncovered the roof of the house where he was. And when they had broken it open, they let down the bed that the paralytic lay in.
2.5: When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, Son, your sins are forgiven you.
2.6: And certain of the scribes were sitting there and thinking in their hearts,
2.7: How does this fellow so blaspheme? Who can forgive sins, but God only?
2.8: And immediately, when Jesus perceived in his spirit that they so questioned in themselves, he said to them, Why do you think such things in your hearts?
2.9: Which is easier to say to the paralytic: Your sins are forgiven you, or to say, Arise, take up your bed and walk?
2.10: But so that you may know that the Son of man has power in earth to forgive sins– He spoke to the paralytic:
2.11: I say to you, arise, and take up your bed, and go your way into your own house.
2.12: And at once he arose, took up the bed, and went out before them all, so that they were all amazed and glorified God, saying, We have never seen anything like this!
2.13: And he went again to the sea side. And all the people gathered to him, and he taught them.
2.14: And as Jesus was passing by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom and said to him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.
2.15: And it came to pass, as Jesus sat at food in Levi’s house, that many publicans and sinners sat at food also with Jesus and his disciples. For there were many who followed him.
2.16: And when the scribes and Pharisees saw him eat with publicans and sinners, they said to his disciples, How is it that he eats and drinks with publicans and sinners?
2.17: When Jesus heard that, he said to them, The whole have no need of the physician, but the sick do. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
2.18: And the disciples of John and the Pharisees used to fast, and so they came and said to him, Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?
2.19: And Jesus said to them, Can the children of a wedding fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
2.20: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them, and then they will fast, in those days.
2.21: Also, no one sows a piece of new cloth onto an old garment, because then the new piece pulls away from the old, and the tear is worse.
2.22: Likewise, no one pours new wine into old wineskins, for if he does, the new wine bursts the skins, and the wine runs out and the vessels are marred. But new wine must be poured into new vessels.
2.23: And it chanced that he was walking through the grain fields in the Sabbath days, and his disciples, as they went their way, began to pluck the ears of grain.
2.24: And the Pharisees said to him, Look, why are they doing on the Sabbath days that which is not lawful?
2.25: And he said to them, Have you never read what David did when he had need and was hungry, both he and those who were with him?
2.26: How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest and did eat the hallowed loaves, which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests only, and gave also to those who were with him?
2.27: And he said to them, The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath.
2.28: Therefore the Son of man is Lord even of the Sabbath day.

3.1: And he entered again into the synagogue, and there was a man there who had a withered hand.
3.2: And they watched him to see if he would heal him on the Sabbath day, so that they might accuse him.
3.3: And he said to the man who had the withered hand, Arise, and stand in the midst.
3.4: And he said to them, Is it lawful to do a good deed on the Sabbath days, or an evil deed? To save life, or to kill? But they held their peace.
3.5: And he looked round about on them angrily, mourning the blindness of their hearts, and said to the man, Stretch forth your hand. And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored fully as whole as the other.
3.6: Then the Pharisees departed, and straightaway assembled a council with Herod’s men against him, so that they might destroy him.
3.7: And Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea. And great crowds followed him from Galilee and from Judea,
3.8: and from Jerusalem and from Idumea and from beyond the Jordan, and also those who dwelt about Tyre and Sidon: great crowds who, when they heard the things he did, came to him.
3.9: And he told his disciples that a boat should be kept at hand for him, because of the people, lest they should throng him.
3.10: For he had healed many, insomuch that they pressed in upon him to touch him, as many as had afflictions.
3.11: And when the unclean spirits saw him, they fell down before him and cried out, saying, You are the Son of God!
3.12: And he charged them strictly not to make him known.
3.13: And he went up into a mountain and called to him whom he wished, and they came to him.
3.14: And he ordained the twelve to be with him, so that he might send them to preach,
3.15: and to have power to heal sicknesses and to cast out devils.
3.16: And he gave Simon the name Peter.
3.17: And he called James, the son of Zebedee, and John, James’ brother, and gave them the name Boanerges, which means Sons of Thunder.
3.18: And there were Andrew and Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon of Canaan,
3.19: and Judas Iscariot, which same also betrayed him. And they came to a house.
3.20: And the people assembled together again, so greatly that they had no opportunity so much as to eat bread.
3.21: And when his family members heard of it, they set out to get him, because they thought he would be beside himself.
3.22: And the scribes who came from Jerusalem said, He has Beelzebub, and by the power of the chief devil he casts out devils.
3.23: And Jesus called them to him and spoke to them in similitudes: How can Satan drive out Satan?
3.24: For if a realm is divided against itself, that realm cannot endure.
3.25: Or if a house is divided against itself, that house cannot continue.
3.26: So if Satan makes insurrection against himself and is divided, he cannot continue, but is at an end.
3.27: No one can enter into a strong man’s house and take away his goods unless he first binds the strong man, and then he plunders his house.
3.28: Truly I say to you, all sins may be forgiven the children of men, and blasphemies with which they blaspheme.
3.29: But he who blasphemes the Holy Spirit may never have forgiveness, but is liable to eternal condemnation.
3.30: ( For they said he had an unclean spirit. )
3.31: Then his mother and his brethren arrived and stood outside, and sent to him and called for him.
3.32: The people were sitting around him, and they said to Jesus, Your mother and your brethren are asking for you outside.
3.33: And he answered them, saying, Who are my mother and my brethren?
3.34: And he looked round about on his disciples, who sat in a circle around him, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren.
3.35: For whosoever does the will of God, he is my brother, my sister, and mother.

4.1: And he began again to teach by the sea side. And there gathered together unto him crowds of people, so greatly that he entered into the boat and sat in it in the sea, and all the people were by the sea side on the shore.
4.2: And he taught them many things in similitudes, and said to them in his lesson:
4.3: Hearken to! Behold, there went out a sower to sow.
4.4: And it happened as he sowed that some seed fell by the wayside, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it up.
4.5: Some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth, and quickly sprang up because it did not have depth of earth;
4.6: but as soon as the sun was up, it caught heat, and because it did not have rooting, withered away.
4.7: And some fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, so that it gave no fruit.
4.8: And some fell upon good ground, and yielded fruit that sprang up and grew, and brought forth: some thirtyfold, some sixtyfold, and some a hundredfold.
4.9: And he said to them, He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
4.10: And when he was alone, those who were around him with the twelve asked him about the similitude.
4.11: And he said to them, To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God. But to those who are outside, all things shall be done in similitudes,
4.12: and when they see, they will see but not discern, and when they hear, they will hear and not understand, lest at any time they should turn; and their sins would be forgiven them.
4.13: And he said to them, Do you not understand this similitude? How then will you understand any other similitudes?
4.15: And those who are by the wayside where the word is sown are those to whom, as soon as they have heard it, Satan comes immediately, and takes away the word that was sown in their hearts.
4.16: And likewise, those who receive the seed on the stony ground are those who, when they have heard the word, at once receive it with gladness,
4.17: yet have no roots in themselves. And so they endure but a time, and once trouble and persecution arise for the word’s sake, they fall immediately.
4.18: And those who receive the seed among the thorns are such as hear the word,
4.19: but the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the hunger for other things, enter in and choke the word, and it is made unfruitful.
4.20: And those who received the seed in good ground are those who hear the word and receive it, and bring forth fruit: some thirtyfold, some sixtyfold, some a hundredfold.
4.21: And Jesus said to the people, Is the candle lighted to be put under a bushel or under the table, and not rather to be put on a candlestick?
4.22: For there is nothing so hid that it will not be revealed, nor so secret but that it may become clear.
4.23: If any person has ears to hear, let him hear.
4.24: And he said to them, Attend with care to what you hear. With the same measure you give, it will be measured back to you. And to you who hear, more will be given.
4.25: For to him who has, it will be given, but from him who has not shall be taken away even what he has.
4.26: And he said, The kingdom of God is like this: it is as if a man sows seed in the ground,
4.27: and sleeps, and rises up night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows up, he knows not how.
4.28: For the earth brings forth fruit of herself: first the blade, then the ears, after that the full grain in the ears.
4.29: And as soon as the fruit is brought forth, immediately the man thrusts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.
4.30: And he said, To what may we liken the kingdom of God? or what comparison can we use?
4.31: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is the least of all seeds that are in the earth.
4.32: But after it is sown, it grows up and is greatest of all shrubs, and bears great branches, so that the birds of the air may dwell under the cover of it.
4.33: And with many such similitudes he preached the word to the people, as they were able to hear it.
4.34: And without similitude he spoke nothing to them. But when they were apart, he expounded all things to his disciples.
4.35: And the same day, when evening was come, he said to them, Let us pass over to the other side.
4.36: And they left the people and took him just as he was in the boat. And there were also with him other boats.
4.37: And there arose a great storm of wind, and it dashed the waves into the boat so that it was full.
4.38: And he was in the stern, asleep on a pillow. And they awoke him and said to him, Teacher, do you not care if we perish?
4.39: And he rose up and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, Peace, and be still! And the wind allayed, and there followed a great calm.
4.40: And he said to them, Why are you so fearful? How is it that you have no faith?
4.41: And they feared exceedingly and said to one another, What manner of man is this? For both wind and sea obey him.

5.1: And they went over to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.
5.2: And when he got out of the boat, there met him out of the graves a man possessed by an unclean spirit,
5.3: who had his dwelling among the graves. And no man could bind him, no, not with chains.
5.4: For he had often been bound with shackles and chains, but he pulled the chains apart and broke the shackles in pieces. Neither could anyone quiet him.
5.5: And always, both night and day, he wailed in the mountains and in the graves, and beat himself with stones.
5.6: When he saw Jesus afar off, he ran and knelt before him,
5.7: and cried out with a loud voice and said, What have I to do with you, Jesus Son of the most high God? I call on you in the name of God not to torment me.
5.8: For Jesus had said to him, Come out of the man, you foul spirit!
5.9: And Jesus asked him, What is your name? He answered, saying, My name is Legion, for we are many.
5.10: And he pressed Jesus urgently not to send them away out of the region.
5.11: And there was there, near to the mountains, a great herd of swine feeding.
5.12: All the devils besought him, saying, Send us into the herd of swine, so that we may enter into them.
5.13: And at once Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out and entered into the swine. And the herd started, and ran headlong into the sea. There were about 2, 000 swine, and they were drowned in the sea.
5.14: And the swineherds fled and told this in the town and in the country. And the people came out to see what had happened,
5.15: and came to Jesus. They saw the man who had been vexed with the fiend and had the legion sitting both clothed and in his right mind, and were afraid.
5.16: And those who had seen it told them what had happened to the man possessed with the devil, and also about the swine.
5.17: And they began to urge Jesus to depart from their shores.
5.18: And when he got into the boat, the man who had been possessed with the devil asked him if he could be with him.
5.19: However Jesus would not allow him, but said to him, Go home to your own house and to your friends, and show them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had compassion on you.
5.20: And he departed and began to tell everywhere in the Ten Cities what great things Jesus had done for him. And all the people marvelled.
5.21: And when Jesus had crossed over again by boat to the other side, crowds of people gathered to him. And he was near to the sea.
5.22: And there came one of the leaders of the synagogue, whose name was Jairus. And when he saw him, he fell down at his feet,
5.23: and besought him greatly, saying, My daughter lies at the point of death. Please come and lay your hand on her, so that she can be saved and live.
5.24: And Jesus went with him, and the crowds followed him and thronged him.
5.25: And there was a certain woman who had been troubled by a flow of blood for twelve years.
5.26: She had endured many things from many physicians, and spent all that she had, and was not helped at all, but grew worse and worse.
5.27: When she heard of Jesus, she penetrated the press behind him and touched his garment.
5.28: For she thought, If I can but touch his clothes, I shall be healed.
5.29: And straightaway her flow of blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of the illness.
5.30: And Jesus immediately felt in himself the power that went out of him, and turned around in the press of people and said, Who touched my clothes?
5.31: And his disciples said to him, You see the people thronging you, and yet you ask, Who touched me?
5.32: And he looked round about to see who had done it.
5.33: The woman feared and trembled ( for she knew what was done within her ), and she came and fell down before him, and told him the truth of everything.
5.34: And he said to her, Daughter, your faith has made you whole. Go in peace, and be healed of your affliction.
5.35: While he was yet speaking, certain people came from the house of the synagogue leader and said, Your daughter is dead; why trouble the Teacher any further?
5.36: As soon as Jesus heard that word spoken, he said to the leader of the synagogue, Be not afraid; only believe.
5.37: And he let no one follow him other than Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
5.38: And he went to the house of the synagogue leader and saw the disturbance, and the people who wept and wailed greatly,
5.39: and went in and said to them, Why do you make this ado, and weep? The maiden is not dead, but sleeping.
5.40: And they laughed him to scorn. Then he put them all out, and took the father and the mother of the maiden and those who were with him, and entered in where the maiden lay.
5.41: He took the maiden by the hand and said to her, Tabitha, cumi! which translated is, Child, I say to you, arise.
5.42: And at once the maiden arose, and she walked on her feet, for she was twelve years of age. And they were astonished at it beyond measure.
5.43: And he charged them strictly that no one should know of it, and said to give her food.

6.1: And he departed from there and went into his own country, and his disciples followed him.
6.2: And when the Sabbath day came, he began to teach in the synagogue. And many who heard him were astonished and said, Where does he have these things from? And what wisdom is this that is given to him? And such miracles that are wrought by his hands!
6.3: Is this not that carpenter – Mary’s son, the brother of James and Joses, and of Judas and Simon? And are his sisters not here with us? And they were offended by him.
6.4: And Jesus said to them, A prophet is not without honour but in his own country, and among his own kin, and among those who are of the same household.
6.5: And he could show no miracles there, except he laid his hands upon a few sick folk and healed them.
6.6: And he marvelled at their unbelief. And he went about by the towns that lay on every side, teaching.
6.7: And he called the twelve and began to send them out two by two, and gave them power over unclean spirits.
6.8: And he commanded them to take nothing for their journey save only a rod – no bag, no bread, no money in their belts –
6.9: but to be shod with sandals, and not to put on two coats.
6.10: And he said to them, Wherever you enter into a house, stay there till you move on from that town.
6.11: And whoever does not receive you or hear you, when you leave there, shake off the dust that is under your feet, for a witness to them. I say truly to you, it will be easier for Sodom and Gomorrah at the day of judgment than for that place.
6.12: And they went out and preached that the people should repent.
6.13: And they cast out many devils, and anointed many who were sick with oil, and healed them.
6.14: And King Herod heard of Jesus ( for his name was spread abroad ) and said, John the Baptist has risen again from death, and therefore miracles are wrought by him.
6.15: Others said, It is Elijah; and some said, It is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.
6.16: But when Herod heard of him, he said, It is John whom I beheaded: he has risen back up from death.
6.17: For Herod himself had sent forth and seized John, and bound him and cast him into prison for the sake of Herodias, who was his brother Philip’s wife. For Herod had married her.
6.18: John said to Herod, It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.
6.19: So Herodias was laying in wait for him, and would have killed him. But she could not,
6.20: because Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just and holy man, and gave him reverence. And he heeded him in many things, and heard him gladly.
6.21: But when an opportune day came, Herod on his birthday put on a supper for the lords, captains, and chief personages of Galilee.
6.22: And the daughter of the said Herodias came in and danced, and pleased Herod and those who sat with him. Then the king said to the maiden, Ask of me what you will, and I will give it to you.
6.23: And he swore to her, Whatever you ask of me, I will give it to you, even up to one half of my kingdom.
6.24: And she went out and said to her mother, What should I ask for? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.
6.25: And the maiden went in straightaway with haste to the king and asked, saying, I would like you to give me right now the head of John the Baptist on a platter.
6.26: And the king was sorry. However, for his oath’s sake, and because of those who sat at supper also, he did not want to put her beside her purpose.
6.27: And immediately the king sent the hangman and commanded John’s head to be brought in. And he went and beheaded him in the prison,
6.28: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the maiden, and the maiden gave it to her mother.
6.29: And when John’s disciples heard of it, they came and took up his body, and put it in a tomb.
6.30: And the apostles gathered themselves together to Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done and what they had taught.
6.31: And he said to them, Come apart into the countryside and rest awhile. For there were so many comers and goers that they had no time so much as to eat.
6.32: And they went by boat out of the way into an isolated place.
6.33: But the people noticed them when they departed, and many recognized him. And they ran there by foot out of all the towns, and got there before them, and came together to him.
6.34: And Jesus went out and saw the crowds of people, and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And he began to teach them many things.
6.35: And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came to him, saying, This is an isolated place, and now the day is far gone.
6.36: Let the people depart so that they can go into the country round about and into the towns and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat.
6.37: He answered and said to them, You give them to eat. And they said to him, Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them to eat?
6.38: He said to them, How many loaves do you have? Go and look. And when they had searched, they said, Five, and two fishes.
6.39: And Jesus directed them to make all the people sit down in groups on the green grass.
6.40: And they sat down here a row and there a row, by hundreds and by fifties.
6.41: And he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looked up to heaven, and blessed, and broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to put before the people. And he divided the two fishes among them all.
6.42: And they all did eat and were satisfied.
6.43: And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments and of the fishes.
6.44: And those who ate were about 5, 000 men.
6.45: And straightaway he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead over the water to Bethsaida while he sent the people away.
6.46: And as soon as he had sent them away, he went apart to a mountain to pray.
6.47: And when evening was come, the boat was in the middle of the sea and he was alone on the land.
6.48: And he saw them having trouble rowing, for the wind was contrary to them. And about the fourth quarter of the night he went out to them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.
6.49: When they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it was a spirit and cried out.
6.50: For they all saw him and were afraid. And immediately he spoke to them and said to them, Be of good cheer, it is I. Be not afraid.
6.51: And he went up to them into the boat, and the wind ceased; and they were greatly amazed in themselves beyond measure, and taken aback.
6.52: For they did not remember about the loaves, because their hearts were blinded.
6.53: And they crossed over and went into the land of Gennesaret, and drew up to anchorage.
6.54: And as soon as they got out of the boat, people quickly recognized Jesus,
6.55: and ran everywhere throughout all the region round about, and began to carry all who were sick in beds to the place where they heard he was.
6.56: And wherever he entered into towns, cities, or villages, they laid their sick in the streets and begged to touch even just the edge of his vesture. And as many as touched him were made well.

7.1: And the Pharisees came together to him, and some of the scribes who came from Jerusalem.
7.2: And when they saw certain of his disciples eat bread with common hands ( that is to say, with unwashed hands ), they complained.
7.3: For the Pharisees and all the Jews, unless they wash their hands often, will not eat, observing the precepts of the elders.
7.4: And when they come from the market, unless they wash, they will not eat. And there are many other things that they have taken upon themselves to observe, such as the washing of cups and pitchers, and of copper pots, and of tables.
7.5: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why do your disciples not walk according to the precepts of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands?
7.6: He answered and said to them, Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written: This people honours me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
7.7: In vain they worship me, teaching doctrines which are nothing but the commandments of men.
7.8: For you lay the commandment of God aside, and observe the precepts of men, such as the washing of pitchers and of cups. And many other suchlike things you do.
7.9: And he said to them, All too well do you cast aside the commandment of God to maintain your own precepts.
7.10: For Moses said, Honour your father and your mother, and whosoever curses father or mother, let him die for it.
